main_text.p: rum in ista ætate Ethnicorum potentiæ æquales ; si non superiores, liquidò demonstrant . Et certè verisimile est, ad Philippi nouissimi Imperatoris exemplum, è fæce & gregario milite, infinitos ; quin & ex ipso Nobilitatis flore, & Aulæ gremio nonnullos ad Christianā fidem accessisse. Inter quos ab Historicis succenturiantur Triphonia Decij Cæsaris Iunioris vxor, Philippus Iunior, & Seuera Augusti Philippi Senioris coniux, Calocerus Cubiculi Imperatoris, vxoris nimirum Decij Senioris præpositus, Parthenius alterius in Aula muneris Princioerius [?]. Secundianus Valeriani Præfecti Assessor, Abdon & Samne in Persia, Subregul[?]i, & denique in exercitu Paramon ob militiam insignis, alijque eius socij, quorum trecenti septuaginta, ob christianam fidem martyrium passi. Interim, quàm formidabile fuerit, adversus Christianos, Imperatoris edictū, apparet partim ex Nysseno, cuius haec sunt verba ; Interea Imperator ad gentium Præsides mittit Edicta, terribiles Supplicij minas in cos [?] statuens, nisi omnibus probris, contumeliis, & cruciati-

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "Princioerius" and "Subreguli" are hard to read in the scan and are marked [?]. The left-hand text is the neighbouring page and is not transcribed. The right margin is empty apart from faint marks, which are not text. Catchword "bus." is the first word of the next page, so the text ends at "cruciati-". The word "cos" is read as printed, with doubt. The strip of fragments at the far left is the neighbouring page edge and is not transcribed. No page number or running head is visible on this part.
